primitives.name: Kick Forward Restrictions
primitives.verbatim_quote: Restrictions When Ball Is Put in Play by Kick Forward.
primitives.assumptions: Ball is kicked forward by the offensive team; yardage threshold of 10 yards into opponent's territory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when an offensive player touches the ball before it travels 10 yards into opponent's territory without being touched by an opponent.

layer2.mapping: Universal Lens - Structural Unification: Models the restriction as a geometric exclusion zone in the half-space of opponent territory, enforcing causality in the temporal sequence of ball contact events.
layer2.telemetry: Measured as the distance traveled by the ball before any offensive player makes contact.

primitives.name: Advance by Snapping Back
primitives.verbatim_quote: Advance of Ball by Player First Receiving It From Snapper-back.
primitives.assumptions: Ball is snapped back to a player; the player attempts to advance the ball beyond the line of scrimmage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when the player carries the ball forward beyond the line of scrimmage without first passing it to another player and having it touched by that player.

layer2.mapping: Universal Lens - Structural Unification: Encodes the rule as a directed graph constraint on the sequence of ball carriers, ensuring compliance with the discrete temporal ordering of passes.
layer2.telemetry: Binary indicator of whether the player advanced the ball directly without satisfying the pass requirement.

primitives.name: No Interference Before Play
primitives.verbatim_quote: (a) Before the ball is put in play no player shall lay his hands upon, or by the use of his hands or arms, interfere with an opponent in such a way as to delay putting the ball in play.
primitives.assumptions: Interference occurs during the pre-snap phase; interference aims to delay the snap.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when a player uses hands or arms to create physical obstruction that prevents the ball from being put in play within the allotted time frame.

layer2.mapping: Universal Lens - Structural Unification: Treats interference as a bounded perturbation of the legal pre-snap configuration space, establishing a clearance radius around each player to prevent collision.
layer2.telemetry: Duration of delay caused by interference, measured in seconds.

primitives.name: Body-Only Obstruction
primitives.verbatim_quote: (Rule 28,A.) No Use of Hands or Arms by Attacking Side.
primitives.assumptions: Post-snap phase; defensive players attempt to block offensive players using only their bodies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when a defender uses hands or arms to create additional leverage or force against an offensive player, violating the body-only constraint.

layer2.mapping: Universal Lens - Structural Unification: Models the allowed interaction as a contact mechanics problem with frictional constraints on the normal and tangential forces at the point of contact between bodies.
layer2.telemetry: Force components applied by hands versus those applied by the body alone, quantified through sensor data or replay analysis.
